- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for risk aversion or market correction.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward revisions to avoid excessive lag.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of declining prices), model often fails to adjust; apply a 2–5% downward bias to next forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to recent sentiment swings; smooth out forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values if sentiment is volatile.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33), model often misses the turn; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for next 2–3 periods.
